observations: Installing the frozen 0.11.1 checkout into a disposable home linked 59 projections and the client's own `codex debug prompt-input` rendered a 37,148-character prompt carrying the harness instructions, every resolved stance and the harness skill root, so effective instructions and discovered skills were read from the client rather than from disk.

A second `harness sync` left the rendered `AGENTS.md` byte-identical, `harness diff --quiet` and `harness doctor` both exited 0 with `drift: none`, and appending one line to the managed `AGENTS.md` made `harness diff` report `modified generated file` with exit 1 and the next sync exit 2 under `Needs your attention`.

Switching `voice`, `commits` and `delegation` in the config and re-syncing changed both the client's rendered prompt (`Voice: answer card`, `Commits stance: off`, `Delegation stance: off`) and its behaviour on one unchanged probe: the commit-message answer went from `fix(parser): add null check` to `Add null check to parser.py` and the delegation answer from "five files do not justify delegation" to "standing delegation is off".

An unknown variant was refused by name with `stance 'voice' has no variant 'not-a-variant'; options: answer-card, off, scannable`, and the rendered `delegation: off` block now reads that a spawn attempted under the stance is denied outright, the 0.11.1 wording change.

A custom `proof-label` dimension authored in a private primitive root was listed by `harness stances --json`, resolved to its external file, rendered into the client's prompt as `<!-- stance proof-label: tagged -->`, and changed the client's native reply from `TAGGED` to `PLAIN` when the selected variant was switched and re-synced.

The precedence chain behaved as documented at the CLI — config default, `HARNESS_STANCE_PROOF_LABEL`, `HARNESS_PROJECT_CONFIG` — an unknown variant was refused by name, and a project config carrying an identity block was refused with `project config may select stances only; user config owns identity, targets and permissions`.

The Codex client's own configuration introspection reported `read-only`/`approvals_reviewer = "user"` under `manual`, `workspace-write`/`auto_review` under `auto` and `danger-full-access` under acknowledged `bypass`, with the superseded `approval_reviewer` key absent in every posture.

One sentinel-file probe per posture matched those settings natively: under `manual` the client refused with `patch rejected: writing is blocked by read-only sandbox; rejected by user approval settings` and no file appeared, while `auto` and acknowledged `bypass` each wrote the sentinel; an unacknowledged `bypass` sync failed with exit 1 naming `danger-full-access` and left the prior posture in place.

With the five harness hooks registered but native hook trust not accepted, a Codex turn raised no hook event at all and the ungated command ran, confirming the catalog's claim that registration is not activation; the hooks were then activated with the client's own `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` flag and a separately registered user hook ran alongside the harness hook on every `PreToolUse` event, logging the tool names `Bash` and `apply_patch` the client delivered.

A grade-3 `git push --force` was blocked by the client with `hook: PreToolUse Blocked` and the harness reason text while the composed user hook still reported `Completed`, a grade-1 recursive removal was correctly allowed, and two allowed turns (a two-file `apply_patch` and a read-only `sed`) reported `hook: PreToolUse Completed` with zero occurrences of `hook: PreToolUse Failed`.

Two isolated role workers ran natively: the gatherer completed with `mode: isolated-cli`, `authority: result data only; no transferred approvals`, read roots limited to the workspace and the checkout, and reported its own write refused by the read-only workspace with no file created; the planner completed with its Review Card artifact published by the harness at `.agent-harness/plans/plan-probe.md` while its out-of-scope second file never appeared.

Both workers recorded `pid` and `pid_start` in `status.json`, and a fixture copy set to `running` with a dead pid and no result was reported by `harness role status` as `orphaned` with the stderr line `the worker process ended without reporting a result`, while the two genuine workers still read `completed`.

Because Codex does not route native spawns, the constrained-role guard was exercised by driving the Codex lifecycle hook directly with synthetic `Agent` events: a named `reviewer` spawn was refused, the same brief re-issued in that session with no role name and with a non-constrained role name was refused with the reason "dropping or changing the role name does not change that", and a spawn whose prompt carried a standalone `harness-role: reviewer` line was refused; a merely paraphrased brief produced no decision, the recorded limitation.

Switching the cost variant from `balanced` to `frugal` and re-syncing rewrote exactly 5 of the 11 Codex role definitions (builder, gatherer, worker-a, worker-b, worker-c) and left 6 byte-identical, moving the non-fixed gatherer from `gpt-5.6-sol`/low to `gpt-5.6-terra`/low while the fixed reviewer row stayed at `gpt-5.6-sol`/high.

The same `workers.resolution()` the `harness role run` path uses resolved each role's model, effort, class source and budget sentence under both variants, and a real completed gatherer worker corroborated it natively: its `status.json` posture block recorded `cost_variant: balanced`, `class_source: cost-row`, `effort_source: cost-row` and a 8,500-token budget, with `harness role status` reporting `effort: low`.
The Codex usage feed is not applicable on this runtime because the client raises none of `UserPromptSubmit`, `SubagentStart` or `SubagentStop`, the reason the catalog itself states.

A trusted disposable repository with a `## Gate` block that appends to its own run log showed the invalidation rule directly: the gate ran once on a clean tree and recorded `status: passed` with a green hash, was not rerun on an unchanged tree (the client reported `hook: Stop Completed` from cache with the run count unmoved), and was rerun after an untracked file appeared and again after a staged edit.

Adding a failure sentinel made the client report `hook: Stop Blocked` and refuse to finish; the session then repaired the failure and the gate reran green, storing a new green hash with `blocks: 0`, so no green result was recorded while the gate was red and the `MAX_BLOCKS` release path was not reached.

One task was carried across three native legs in one repository — Claude Code saved revision 1, a Codex session read it with `harness task show`, did its `next_steps` entry and saved revision 2, and a second Claude Code session read that, finished the remaining step and saved revision 3 — with `calc.py` ending with all four helpers and each record carrying `authority: data only; approvals and native permissions must be established in this session`, so no approval crossed either handoff.

Saving against an already-used revision was refused cleanly with exit 1, no stdout, and a single stderr line `task revision changed since --revision 1; read the current task, then save against its revision` carrying no traceback and no absolute path; appending to a tracked file turned the task `stale` with `working tree changed after handoff`, and a byte-exact restore returned it to `current`.

Installing over a home that already held a hand-written Codex `config.toml`, a personal `AGENTS.md`, an unrelated Claude `settings.json` env key and a session file was refused with exit 2 and `unmanaged file; adopt explicitly before replacing it`, leaving the user's file byte-identical; `--adopt --adopt-codex` then merged only the harness-owned key and preserved the user's `model` line and `[tui]` table.

Hand-editing an owned key produced `modified owned key: ~/.codex/config.toml:project_doc_fallback_filenames` with diff exit 1 and a sync exit 2 that preserved the user's value, and replacing a managed skill link with a real file was refused with `exists and is not a harness link; pass --adopt to move it aside`.

`harness uninstall` unlinked every projection, emptied Codex `hooks.json` to `{"hooks": {}}`, restored the adopted `AGENTS.md` byte-for-byte by SHA256, left the unrelated env key and the session file untouched, reported both user-changed items as preserved conflicts, removed `rules/harness-stances/` and every `skills/harness-*` entry rather than leaving them empty, and ended `uninstalled; personal files, config and the checkout are untouched`.

The pinned BMad 6.12.0 runtime installed clean into the framework checkout, `harness bmad check` reported 0 drift, `harness bmad apply` wrote the three user templates, and resolving the code-review customization with the framework checkout as project root produced all four review layers with `harness role run` present four times and each layer's brief beginning with its `harness-role: reviewer` or `harness-role: spec-reviewer` marker line.

The review workflow ran in the background from the framework checkout against a git worktree carrying two seeded defects, wrote its diff inside that worktree, and routed its three applicable layers as isolated `harness role run` workers strictly one at a time: no two workers overlapped, and each reached `status: completed` with `mode: isolated-cli`, worker state, `pid`/`pid_start`, `model: gpt-5.6-luna`, `effort: high` and a `result.md` returning findings.

The session triaged those returned findings into `REVIEW.md` with three patch findings and two deferred findings, reporting both seeded defects — `apply_discount` treating `percent` as a fraction and `average([])` raising `ZeroDivisionError` — while the fourth layer, the acceptance auditor, was skipped by the recipe's own no-specification condition rather than by any routing failure.
